answer: A farm thus spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the pearl quota and the tundra admission check. Because the inlet audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. Admission is capped at 7 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. That is 35 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
